purpose: Test whether an RDG-style symmetry selector can preserve a typed discrete Maxwell complex and expose the obstruction created by an untyped repair.

selector.group: Z2 generated by one-cell translation in x on the N=2 periodic complex
selector.definition: Pi_k=(I+T_k)/2 on every cochain degree; Q_k=I-Pi_k
selector.interpretation: Haar averaging is a gauge-compatible admissibility selector only because the group acts by cochain maps on every degree.

gaugeAndTopology.conclusion: The three constant axial one-forms span the H1 remainder: they are curl-free but not periodic gradients and require Wilson-period coordinates.

untypedSelectorCounterexample.definition: identity on C0/C3 and keep-only-x-component projection on C1/C2
untypedSelectorCounterexample.conclusion: An idempotent selector on each carrier space need not be a chain map; this one turns a pure gauge d0 chi into nonzero selected curvature.

dynamicTransport.map: one-cell x translation used as a topology-preserving geometry update
dynamicTransport.conclusion: This update transports the full complex functorially. Arbitrary repair/projection does not inherit that property.

topologyChange.conclusion: A torus-to-contractible carrier change removes three H1 Wilson sectors and three H2 flux sectors; no degreewise chain isomorphism can hide that event.

verdict: The fixed-complex bridge passes exactly for a symmetry action that is a cochain action. Haar projection alone is insufficient: admissibility must commute with the differential, preserve harmonic records, and use typed transport when geometry changes.
